page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.2xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the high-clock-speed family, designed around a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Built on the KVM hypervisor with the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). Vector instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, complemented by cryptographic AES acceleration. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, operating entirely with remote storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfc6.2xlarge solidly in the average tier across general compute and memory tasks, matching typical mid-tier cloud virtual machines. It delivers a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,795.0 and a single-core score of 1,244.0, with PassMark measuring an overall CPU score of 8,939.31. Memory operations show robust transfer capability, sustaining 49.31 GB/sec read and 35.82 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks, along with 7.45 million Redis SET operations per second. However, heavier multi-threaded compression drops below average, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the bottom 25% at 37.32 GB/sec.

The primary limitation is constrained memory capacity and the absence of discrete accelerator hardware. While small-scale AI workloads run competently, recording 518.12 tokens/sec prompt processing on a 135M parameter model, medium models such as 7B parameters struggle significantly, yielding weak generation rates of 6.44 tokens/sec and falling into the bottom 10% for prompt processing. Given its dedicated core allocation and clock profile, the server offers efficient compute density for standard backend operations without incurring the overhead of large memory arrays or GPU attachments.

The ecs.hfc6.2xlarge is suited for moderately compute-intensive tasks that do not exceed a 16 GB memory footprint. Effective use cases include web serving, software build pipelines, CI/CD runners, batch encoding, and microservice infrastructure.
